members.name: Dr Moritz Weiss
members.position: Senior Lecturer of International Relations and European Studies
members.bio: Moritz Weiss (he) is Senior Lecturer of International Relations and European Studies at LMU Munich. He is Action Chair of 'NetSec'; and also Principal Investigator of the projects ‘The Making of National Security’ (funded by the Fritz Thyssen Stiftung) and 'Big Tech and Regulatory Capture' (funded by the Mercator Foundation Switzerland). His research focuses on the governance of European and international security as well as the political economy of digital technologies. He was a visiting professor of international politics at the Leibniz University Hannover and the LMU Munich as well as a Jean-Monnet-Fellow at the EUI in Florence. His research was published in Security Studies, Contemporary Security Policy, Journal of Global Security Studies, Governance, Review of International Political Economy, International Studies Review, Journal of Common Market Studies, West European Politics and Journal of European Public Policy.

members.name: Mr Eugenio Sánchez
members.bio: Eugenio Sánchez is a PhD Researcher at the Center for International Studies (CERI), Sciences Po Paris, where he is also co-founder and co-coordinator of the Research Group on International Political Economy. His two main areas of academic research focus on (1) how countries in Europe's periphery manage their dependency on foreign capital in key sectors, and (2) how state-business relations shape modern great power competition. In his policy work, Eugenio has primarily dealt with the analysis of Foreign Direct Investment screening in strategic sectors. He has teaching experience in Political Science and International Relations at the BA and MA levels.

members.name: Dr John N.T. Helferich
members.bio: John Helferich is a Lecturer in Politics at Hertford College and a researcher with the Oxford Global Security Programme. His research focuses on European security and transformations in international order. He holds a Doctor of Philosophy (DPhil) in International Relations from the University of Oxford and a Master’s degree in International Security (summa cum laude) from Sciences Po. His dissertation on EU defence integration won the PSA Best Dissertation Prize in International Relations. He chairs the Working Group on Transfer of Knowledge within the COST Action Networking European Security Knowledge and serves as a board member of the European Initiative for Security Studies (EISS).
themes: Political psychology, public opinion and decision-making

members.name: Dr Chiara Ruffa
members.affiliation: Sciences Po, Center for International Studies (CERI)

members.name: Dr Arthur Laudrain
members.affiliation: ETH Zürich, Center for Security Studies
members.position: Team Lead & Senior Researcher, Cyber Security
members.bio:
Arthur specialises in election interference, disinformation, subversion, and military cyber operations. Previously, he was the Richard Lounsbery US-France Security Fellow at Stanford CISAC, and a Research Associate in Cyber Diplomacy at the Department of War Studies at King's College London. He is a member of the Management Committee of NetSec (Networking European Security Knowledge), a European Cooperation in Science and Technology project. He also maintains affiliations with Stanford CISAC and King's College London. Arthur has a wide profesionnal experience spanning think-tanks (CSS 2017; IISS 2019; HCSS 2022), consulting (Oxford Analytica, ISTARI), and government projects.

He obtained his DPhil from the University of Oxford (Wolfson College), and holds an MA (London) and LLM (Leiden). He is an Associate of King's College (AKC) and Fellow of the Higher Education Academy (FHEA).

members.name: Mr Felix Kösterke
members.bio:
Felix Koesterke joined the Egmont Institute in September 2025 as a Research Fellow in the Europe in the World Programme. He is a doctoral candidate at Ghent University and part of the MSCA-funded doctoral network Contested EU Foreign Policy in an Era of Geopolitics (EUFOG). His research focuses on European Union grand strategy and Europe’s role in a changing international order.

Previously, he worked at the Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung in Berlin on Germany’s Zeitenwende, and held positions at Interpeace Europe, the German Bundestag, and the German Federal Foreign Office. He studied Political Science and Communication in Mainz and Strasbourg and holds a Master’s degree in International Security from Sciences Po Paris.

members.name: Ms Meret Steybe
members.affiliation: ETH Zürich, Center for Security Studies
members.bio:
Meret Steybe is a security policy researcher at the Center for Security 
Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich, where she works on German and European security 
policy, institutional impact assessment, and strategic planning. 

Previously, Meret served as a policy advisor for the Bundestag's Study Commission 
on "Lessons from Afghanistan for Germany's Comprehensive International 
Engagement in the Future," where she developed cross-party positions and 
coordinated strategic negotiations. She has deep expertise in translating 
complex security challenges into actionable policy recommendations.

Meret holds a bachelor's degree in European Studies with a minor in European and International Law, and a master's degree in European Public Affairs, both from Maastricht University.

members.name: Anna Pagnacco
members.affiliation: ETH Zürich, Center for Security Studies
members.bio:
Anna Pagnacco is a Researcher with the Cyber Security Team at the Center for Security Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich.

Previously part of NATO HQ’s Cyber Strategy and Policy team, Anna has worked in military and civilian cyber defence at the NATO Digital Staff and Cyber and Digital Transformation Division; tracked cyber regulation with a focus on China at Digital Policy Alert; and led research on data localisation and Internet standardisation at Oxford Information Labs. Their research interests include the protection of cyber infrastructure, supply chain security, non-traditional cyber effects, and the use of cyber in military operations.

Anna holds an Honours Master’s in Political Science from Sant’Anna School of Advanced Studies (Pisa) with a focus on international security and the Law of Armed Conflict; a Master’s in International Relations from the Cesare Alfieri faculty of Political Science (Florence) including a semester-long visiting period at University College London; and a Bachelor’s in Political Science from the University of Pisa.

members.name: Ms Rusudan Zabakhidze
members.bio:
Rusudan Zabakhidze is a PhD Candidate in the Department of War Studies at the Swedish Defence University. Her research focuses on war preparedness and civilian voluntary defence mobilisations in Georgia. Alongside her doctoral work, she teaches courses on civil-military relations, war and conflict, and urban warfare.
Rusudan has strong analytical, project management, and outreach skills, demonstrated through her experience working in large-scale international research projects funded by programmes such as Jean Monnet and the European Research Council. Prior to her doctoral studies, she worked at the Council for European Studies at Columbia University on the issues of securitisation of ethnic minorities and migrants and the rise of xenophobia in the European Union. She also served as a research assistant on the ETHNICGOODs project, contributing to the construction of a dataset on nation-building strategies and collecting qualitative data on public goods provision and political violence in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Hungary, North Macedonia, and Kosovo. In addition, she has worked on the Black Sea security and European integration issues through various research fellowships.
Rusudan holds an MSc in International Security, Intelligence, and Strategic Studies from the University of Glasgow, Dublin City University, and Charles University in Prague, and a BA in International Relations from Tbilisi State University.

members.name: Dr Alexandra Brankova
members.bio:
Alexandra Brankova is a postdoctoral fellow at the Department of Political Science working on a project about Geopolitical Narratives. Alexandra is also an affiliated researcher at the Institute for Russian and Eurasian studies, Uppsala University. She holds a PhD degree in Media and Communications from Uppsala University.

Her research interests include geopolitical narratives, identity construction, international relations, digital media, nationalism studies, great power politics, and ontological security.

members.name: Lucian Bumeder
members.bio: Lucian Bumeder works as a researcher in the Arms Control and Emerging Technologies Research group. Since April 2023, he has been part of the Challenges to Deep Cuts project, where he coordinates the Young Deep Cuts Commission. Prior to his time at IFSH, he worked as a policy aide in the office of Merle Spellerberg who serves on the on the Defense Committee of the German Bundestag as well as for the transnational journalist network n-ost. Lucian Bumeder studied Political Science (B.A.) and International Relations (M.A.) at Freie Universität Berlin and at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO) with an interim stay at Tulane University in New Orleans.

members.name: Mr Pieter Zhao
members.bio: Pieter W.G. Zhao is a PhD candidate and junior lecturer at the Department of History at Erasmus University Rotterdam, where his doctoral research is funded by the competitive NWO PhD in the Humanities Grant (2024). His project examines how nonmilitary and irregular actors have shaped maritime warfare and security throughout history, and how these historical dynamics can inform contemporary debates on maritime strategy and security. In 2026, he was a Visiting PhD Fellow at the Department of War Studies, King's College London, hosted by Prof. Christopher Kinsey and the Forum for Private Security Research. Pieter holds a BA and an MA in History from Erasmus University Rotterdam, specialising in the history of international relations and maritime history, as well as a second Master's degree in International Security from Sciences Po, with concentrations in Strategic Studies, Asian Studies, and Intelligence Studies. He completed part of his coursework at Johns Hopkins SAIS in Washington, DC, focusing on US-China relations, maritime security, and nuclear proliferation. Alongside his academic work, Pieter has served as a Nonresident Fellow at the Irregular Warfare Initiative and a Maritime Leadership Fellow at the Council on Geostrategy. His work has appeared in the Naval War College Review, Comparative Strategy, the European Journal of East Asian Studies, Small Wars Journal, Militaire Spectator, and The Strategy Bridge, and he has provided historical and strategic commentary for Dutch outlets including NOS, BNR Nieuwsradio, and de Volkskrant. Happy to connect with scholars interested in historical approaches to contemporary security challenges, applied history, the maritime domain, and the Indo-Pacific region, with a particular focus on China.

members.name: Mr Saurav Narain
members.bio:
Saurav Narain is a Marie-Curie PhD Candidate with the war, peace and justice research group at ISGA. His research interests are in the fields of EU Counterterrorism, United Nations and Local Peacekeeping. He is funded by Horizon Europe’s MSCA EU-GLOCTER project. 

He has completed Erasmus Mundus International Master in Security, Intelligence and Security Studies (IMSISS) degree from University of Glasgow, Dublin City University and Charles University, Prague and additionally an MA in International Relation from Leiden University.
themes: EU, UN and other international organisations

members.name: Mr Archishman Goswami
members.bio:
Archishman is a DPhil International Relations candidate at the University of Oxford. His research interests lie in the field of security and strategic studies, with a particular focus on emerging technologies and intelligence in international politics. He also specialises in Indian foreign policy and national security posture in a changing world order.

Archishman's doctoral research at Oxford examines intelligence diplomacy and its use as a device of modern statecraft. In particular, he investigates how normative conventions and the pursuit of material outcomes animates the pursuit of clandestine diplomacy and intelligence liaison, shaping how and why they are used by states as a policy option.

At present, Archishman is a Non-Resident Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation, India's premier think tank focused on geopolitics and geoeconomics. Prior to his time in Oxford, he studied at King’s College London, being awarded First-Class (Hons) for both his BA in International Relations and MA in National Security Studies. He conducted research on Israel’s role in the Second Libyan Civil War (2014-2019), and ISIS’ practice of counterintelligence for his undergraduate and Master's theses respectively.

members.name: Dr Mattia Sguazzini
members.bio: Mattia Sguazzini is a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the University of Genoa and a 2026–2027 Virtual Routes European Cybersecurity Fellow. He is also an Adjunct Lecturer at Sciences Po’s Menton campus and at the University of Pavia. He was previously a Visiting Research Fellow at the Centre for Security, Diplomacy and Strategy (CSDS) at the Brussels School of Governance, Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB). He holds a PhD in Security and Strategic Studies from the interdisciplinary doctoral programme in Security, Risk and Vulnerability at the University of Genoa, where his dissertation examined the cybersecurity policy design space of EU member states. His research sits at the intersection of cybersecurity governance, digital sovereignty, and the political economy of security in Europe. He also has a strong methodological interest in text-as-data approaches in the social sciences, particularly in the use and fine-tuning of large language models for policy analysis.

members.name: Mr Francesco Canossi
members.bio:
Francesco Canossi is a Franco-Italian defence strategist and industrial engineer working at the intersection of security policy, technology, and defence-industrial strategy.
Trained as a mechanical and industrial engineer at the Università di Bologna and Politecnico di Milano, he subsequently worked as a strategy consultant at Kearney's Aerospace and Defence practice, advising governments and multinational prime contractors across Europe, the Middle East, and the United States on defence localization, industrial cooperation, and emerging technology. He holds a minority equity stake and advisory role in MIRAI Robotics, a European maritime autonomy startup.
His research and writing focus on European defence industrial policy, maritime security, and the governance of emerging technologies within alliance contexts. His essay on undersea cable vulnerability and hybrid threats was awarded second prize in the First Sea Lord's Essay Competition at the Sea Power Conference 2025, presented by Admiral Sir Gwyn Jenkins. He publishes through the Council on Geostrategy's The Broadside, among others.
Francesco holds fellowships and affiliations with the Institut des Hautes Études de Défense Nationale, the Centre d'Études Stratégiques de la Marine, the NATO Defence College Next Generation Futures programme, the Council on Geostrategy Maritime Leaders Programme, and RUSI NextGen. He serves as a mentor and panel evaluator for NATO DIANA and is a participant in the Spinelli Forum 2026. He holds dual French and Italian citizenship and is a native speaker of both languages, alongside fluent English.

members.name: Dr Gil Baram
members.bio:
Dr. Gil Baram researches how AI is reshaping the cybercrime and cyber conflict landscape, focusing on what the shift means for incident response, attribution, and cross-sector coordination. Over the past two years, she has led tabletop exercises in Berkeley, Singapore, and Tel Aviv, bringing together senior practitioners from government, law enforcement, critical infrastructure, and the technology sector to stress-test how existing playbooks hold up against AI-accelerated operations. 
She is a Senior Lecturer (Associate Professor) at Bar-Ilan University and a non-resident research scholar at UC Berkeley’s Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity (CLTC). 
She advises industry, government, and international organizations on AI-enabled cyber threats, cyber diplomacy and policy.

members.name: Ms Sara Russo
members.bio: Sara Russo is a Ph.D. candidate in Defence and Security Studies at the Centre for Higher Defence Studies (CASD) and the University of Turin, where her research focuses on cognitive warfare, strategic communication, influence dynamics, leadership, and organizational resilience. Her work explores how influence operates across social, organizational, and technological systems, with particular attention to the evolving challenges posed by hybrid threats, information environments, and emerging forms of conflict.

members.name: Ms Yanina Shved-Dogrul
members.bio:
I am a Teaching Assistant, researcher, and Ph.D. candidate in International Relations at Istanbul Nişantaşı University. Born in Ukraine to a family of Ukrainian and Polish heritage, I hold Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Philology and a Master's degree in Polish Studies from Istanbul University. My thesis, Istanbul Reflected by the Poles from the 18th to the 21st Centuries, explored the historical and cultural connections between Türkiye, Poland, and Ukraine.
My research interests include European security, regional cooperation, international relations, and the Black Sea region. I have presented papers on Turkish-Polish-Ukrainian relations at academic conferences and am actively engaged in interdisciplinary research on Europe and its neighbourhood.
Alongside my academic work, I teach at Boğaziçi University and the Turkish National Defence University. Through my research and teaching, I seek to contribute to dialogue and cooperation across European and regional contexts.

members.name: Mr Marco Cifra
members.bio: Marco Cifra is a Ph.D. student in Defence and Security Studies at the Centre for Higher Defence Studies (CASD) in Rome, specializing in international law with a focus on space law, international humanitarian law, and the regulation of artificial intelligence in military contexts. His research examines the legal implications of AI-driven decision support systems in warfare, with particular attention to targeting processes, the principles of proportionality and precaution, and the concept of meaningful human control.

members.name: Prof. Seyithan Ahmet Ates
members.bio:
Dr. Ates is a Full Professor of Economics at the Ankara University of Social Sciences (ASBU). As an academic and practitioner, his research examines the intersection of innovation, structural competitiveness, and socio-technical transformation, with a primary focus on defense economics and the global defense industry.

Dr. Ates’s current research centers on the diffusion and synergy between the defense and civilian sectors, particularly the evolution and integration of dual-use technologies. He extensively analyzes the transition of defense ecosystems from buyer-client models to competitor-exporter paradigms, specifically within NATO countries and emerging defense markets. His work explores sovereign defense capabilities, military-civil fusion, and NATO interoperability, addressing the shifting geopolitical power dynamics that shape modern security. 

He holds a PhD in Social and Economic Sciences from the Vienna University of Technology (TU Wien) and earned his undergraduate and graduate degrees from the Vienna University of Economics and Business (WU). His academic journey includes a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University, Oxford University, International Institute for Advanced System Analysis, Austria (IIASA) and National Taiwan University.

members.name: Dr Wendy He
members.affiliation: College of Fellows, University of Tübingen
members.bio: Wendy He is an interdisciplinary scholar of international relations, specialising in U.S.-China relations, strategic studies, and political psychology. She holds a PhD in International Relations from the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore. She is currently a Global Encounters Fellow at the University of Tübingen’s College of Fellows and a Research Fellow with the Military Studies Programme at RSIS. Previously, she was a Hans J. Morgenthau Fellow in Grand Strategy at the Notre Dame International Security Center, University of Notre Dame, and a visiting researcher at National Taiwan University and the University of Washington. Her research examines how cognitive and social psychological dynamics shape strategic judgment in war and crisis decision-making. Her book project, The Confidence Trap, develops a theory of how leaders and advisers assess the credibility of military threats, showing how confidence can enable decisive leadership while also distorting advice-seeking, threat assessment, and strategic judgment. This research agenda has been recognised by the International Studies Association’s Carl Beck Award in 2026 and the Inter-University Seminar on Armed Forces and Society Graduate Student Paper Award in 2025.
themes: Political psychology, public opinion and decision-making

members.name: Prof. Nikolaos Tzifakis
members.bio: Nikolaos Tzifakis holds a Jean Monnet Chair in EU Foreign Policy and the Western Balkans and is a Professor of International Relations at the Department of Political Science and International Relations of the University of the Peloponnese. He is the Coordinator of the “Empowering the Geopolitical EU in the Eastern Neighborhood and the Western Balkans (GEO-POWER-EU)” Horizon Europe Project (2024–2027). He is also a Visiting Professor at the College of Europe (in Tirana) and at the European Regional Master (ERMA) in “Democracy and Human Rights in South-East Europe” (University of Bologna/University of Sarajevo), and a member of Balkans in Europe Policy Advisory Group (BiEPAG). His research interests include EU enlargement policy and geopolitical competition in the Western Balkans.
keywords: Geopolitical Competition in the Western Balkans

members.name: Prof. Mark Rhinard
members.bio: Mark Rhinard is Professor of International Relations at Stockholm University. He earned his MPhil and PhD degrees from Cambridge University and taught at Oxford University before being awarded a postdoctoral fellowship at Leiden University. His research focuses on the institutional contexts of international cooperation, with particular attention to governance resilience in the face of transboundary security threats such as terrorism, pandemics, and climate-related disasters. He serves as Research Director at the Swedish Institute of International Affairs (UI) and is an external advisor to the European Policy Centre in Brussels.
themes: Crisis management and critical systems resilience

members.name: Dr Linde Desmaele
members.position: Assistant Professor of Intelligence and Security
members.bio:
Linde Desmaele is an Assistant Professor of Intelligence and Security at Leiden University. 
Her work sits at the intersection of international relations and security studies, with a focus on nuclear politics, US alliances and European security. Previously, Linde was a Stanton Nuclear Security Fellow in the MIT Security Studies Program and a Belgian American Educational Foundation Postdoctoral Fellow at Columbia University. She holds a PhD from the Free University of Brussels, for which she received the 2022 Global Strategy PhD Prize, jointly awarded by the European Security and Defence College (European External Action Service) and the Egmont Royal Institute for International Relations. She also holds an MA from Seoul National University’s Graduate School of International Studies and another MA from KU Leuven.

members.name: Dr Alexander Lanoszka
members.bio: Alexander Lanoszka is Associate Professor in the Department of Political Science and the Balsillie School of International Affairs at the University of Waterloo in Canada. He is also a visiting professor at the College of Europe in Natolin, Poland. His research addresses alliance politics and military strategy, with a focus on East-Central Europe. He has published in leading peer-reviewed journals such as International Affairs, International Security, International Studies Quarterly, and Security Studies. His books include Atomic Assurance: The Alliance Politics of Nuclear Proliferation (Cornell, 2018) and Military Alliances in the Twenty-First Century (Polity, 2022). He received his Ph.D. from Princeton University.

members.name: Dr Julia Carver
members.bio: Dr. Julia Carver is an Assistant Professor in ISGA’s Cybersecurity Governance Research Group. Previously, she was a Postdoctoral Researcher with the Hague Programme on International Cyber Security. She earned her DPhil in International Relations at the University of Oxford (Nuffield College) as the recipient of an ESRC/UKRI studentship. Prior to the DPhil, she completed an MPhil in Politics (European Governance) at Oxford with Distinction, and a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) at Queen's University in Canada, specialising in Politics and Modern European Languages. Prior to joining Leiden, Julia was a 2024–2025 European Cyber Security Fellow at Virtual Routes, a Research Associate at Oxford’s Department of Computer Science, and a Research Fellow at Oxford’s Changing Character of War Centre. At Oxford, she also served as a Lecturer in Politics at Magdalen College, where she taught undergraduate politics for three years. In 2021, she founded the Cyber Strategy and Information Operations research group (now the Oxford Technology & Security Nexus), affiliated with Oxford’s Changing Character of War Centre and Nuffield College. Julia has collaborated with national governments on cybersecurity, defence, and strategic policy, including governance responses to large-scale ransomware attacks and net assessment.

members.name: Dr Sophie Enos-Attali
members.bio:
After a PhD on the security policies of some European "neutral" countries, I've bee working for several years both on the security policies of Nordic countries and on the security policies of European "neutral" countries in the framework of the war in Ukraine. 
I teach International Relations and Political Science at the Catholic University of Paris and I am a associate researcher at Centre Thucydide (Université Panthéon-Assas) and editorial coordinator of L'Année des relations internationales, a yearly French-speaking journal dedicated to International Relations.

members.name: Ms Yijun Xu
members.bio: Xu Yijun is a PhD researcher at Freie Universität Berlin specializing in peace studies and Korean studies. Her research explores how transnational experiences shape young Koreans’ visions of peace, comparing perspectives between those living in South Korea and Germany through Q-methodology. From October 2024 to April 2025, she has been visiting PhD at the Institute for Peace and Unification Studies at Seoul National University. In the 2025/26 winter semester, she leads an X-Student Research Group titled “What Does Peace Mean to Us? Young Germans Reflect on Peace in a Post-Unification Society.” Xu holds a bachelor’s degree in German Studies from China and a master’s degree in Political Science from South Korea. Her current work contributes to advancing local and non-Western approaches in peace research.

members.name: Ms Vasiliki Plessia Aravani
members.affiliation: Vienna School of International Studies, University of Vienna
members.position: Marie Curie Early Stage Researcher, PhD Candidate
members.bio: Vasiliki Plessia Aravani is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Early Stage Researcher and PhD candidate at the Diplomatische Akademie Wien. She is also a Visiting Researcher at the Centre for Security, Diplomacy and Strategy (CSDS) at Vrije Universiteit Brussel. Her doctoral research examines how emerging technologies and science and technology cooperation are transforming military alliances and security partnerships, with a particular focus on the Atlantic security space and its evolving connections with the Indo-Pacific. She holds a Master’s degree in International Security from Sciences Po Paris and has previously worked with NATO’s Science and Technology Organisation and the OECD. Her research interests include transatlantic and Indo-Pacific security, emerging technologies, alliance politics, military innovation, and tech diplomacy.

members.name: Ms Teodora Stoicescu
members.affiliation: National University of Political Studies and Public Administration
members.bio: Teodora Stoicescu is a PhD candidate at the Department of Political Science at National University of Political Studies and Public Administration, where her doctoral research is fully funded. Her project examines how feminism and international jurisprudence are working in armed conflicts, with focus on sexual violence as a weapon of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ukraine and Armenia. Her research interests are in the fields of Feminist Theories, Sexual Violence during war and outside of war, Jurisprudence, Reconciliation, Transitional Justice and Humanitarian Aid. Teodora holds a BA in Political Science, specialising in Democrating Backsliding in Europe and the reality of post-democratic states, as well as a Master's degree in Security and Diplomacy at the National University of Political Studies and Public Administration, specialising in war crimes against women during the Bosnian War and the international response. Teodora is interested in connecting with scholars interested in feminist theories, gender-based violence, sexual violence as a weapon of war, transitional justice, international jurisprudence, security studies, diplomacy and geostrategy.

members.name: Dr Marko Kovačević
members.affiliation: University of Belgrade, Faculty of Political Science
members.bio: I am an Assistant Professor of International Security at the University of Belgrade, Faculty of Political Science. My research and teaching focus on international relations theory, critical security studies, European security, small states, and academic writing. In my PhD (2021), I examined identity-role construction in the foreign and security policies of small states at the UN, with a focus on Yugoslavia, Serbia, and Croatia. My recent work explores regional security cooperation in the Western Balkans and Eastern European candidacies for elected UN bodies. I led WP3 on Regional Security Initiatives within the MIND project (2022-2025) funded by the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia and currently contribute to the Horizon Europe project Geo-Power-EU (2024-2027). Some of my articles have been published in Foreign Policy Analysis, Journal of Political Science Education, European Political Science, The Hague Journal of Diplomacy, Journal of International Relations and Development, Journal of Contemporary European Studies and Journal of Intervention and Statebuilding, including the chapters in edited volumes by Central European University Press, Routledge, and Springer. I am a member of ISA, ACUNS, EISA, ECPR, CEEISA, and EISS, co-editor of the Journal of Regional Security, and head of the Centre for International Security at the Faculty of Political Science (since 2026).
keywords: Small States' Foreign and Security Policy
canonical_keywords: Small states' foreign and security policy

members.name: Dr Gesine Weber
members.affiliation: ETH Zürich, Center for Security Studies
members.bio:
Dr. Gesine Weber is a Senior Researcher in the Global Security team at the Center for Security Studies (CSS). Her research interests include European security and defense in the context of global powershifts, grand strategy, the global order, and Europe–China relations.

Before joining the CSS, Gesine was a Research Fellow at the Paris office of the German Marshall Fund of the United States (GMF), a transatlantic think tank. In 2024, she spent six months as a Visiting Scholar at Columbia University’s Arnold A. Saltzman Institute in New York, conducting research with a Fulbright-Schuman scholarship. Previously, she worked as a Research Consultant for the Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung in Shanghai and as policy advisor focusing on defense policy in the German Bundestag. She has also been an Associate Researcher at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR) and the Centre for Grand Strategy at King’s College London, as well as a Non-Resident Hans J. Morgenthau Fellow at the Notre Dame Center for International Security.

Gesine regularly advises government bodies and international organizations in Europe and the United States and publishes and comments in European and international media, including Le Monde, Deutsche Welle, War on the Rocks, BBC, and NZZ, as well as on her Substack newsletter Geopolitical Europe. In 2024, her commitment to translating academic research into policy practice and public debate was recognized with the Research Impact Prize of the Faculty of Social Science and Public Policy at King’s College London.

Gesine holds a PhD in Defence Studies from King’s College London, master’s degrees from Sciences Po Paris and Freie Universität Berlin, and a bachelor’s degree from the Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg.
themes: EU, UN and other international organisations

members.name: Mr Fabio Iguavita Duarte
members.bio: Strategic Intelligence Analyst at the Czech Technical University (ČVUT–UCEEB), within the Security of Strategic Infrastructure team, and a PhD candidate in Political Science at Charles University. He holds degrees with honours in International Relations and Geography–Development Studies, with additional training in Global Terrorism and Cybersecurity. His work covers hybrid threat mapping affecting EU/NATO, systems resilience, and tabletop exercise scenario design. He developed a vectorial analytical model for hybrid threat classification, presented at ESSC 2026 (Stockholm), jointly organised by NetSec, EISS, and Stockholm University. He has participated in ECPR, ISA, CEISA, CES, and South America-focused conferences at Ludovika University of Public Service (Budapest), conducted teaching mobility at the University of Sarajevo, and lectures on Geopolitics and Security in Latin America at Charles University. His current focus engages critical infrastructure vulnerability, organised crime, great power strategy, and instability dynamics from the Western Hemisphere, bringing disciplinary and geographic perspectives relevant to Europe's defence and strategic autonomy.
themes: Crisis management and critical systems resilience

members.name: Ms Isabelle Haynes
members.bio: Isabelle Haynes is a PhD candidate in the Area Studies program at the Institute of International Studies, Faculty of Social Sciences, Charles University. She is a Junior Research at the Peace Research Centre Prague and the PhD student on the ERC-project MICROCODE. She holds an MSc in Migration Studies and an MPhil in International Relations from the University of Oxford, as well as a BA in Archaeology and Classics from University College London. Isabelle has professional experience across the public, private, and academic sectors, including roles at UN Tourism, the UK Ministry of Defence, the Nuffield Centre for Experimental Social Science, and SouthWest Archaeology.
themes: Political psychology, public opinion and decision-making

members.name: Ms Anna Seliverstova
members.bio: I am a PhD candidate in Political Science at Linnaeus University, Sweden. My research focuses on EU enlargement, democratic backsliding, and the politics of reform in the Western Balkans, with a particular focus on Serbia. More broadly, I am interested in EU external governance, conditionality, civil society, and how candidate countries navigate the accession process.
themes: EU, UN and other international organisations

members.name: Ms Kara Schneider
members.bio:
Kara Schneider is a researcher and policy professional specializing in the intersection of human rights, emerging technologies, and international security. She is completing an MSc in Human Rights and Data Science at The American University of Paris and has worked with UNESCO, International Bridges to Justice, and Lawyers Without Borders on projects related to AI governance, digital rights, access to justice, and international law.

Her current research examines the impact of generative AI on the integrity of mass violence and genocide testimony, with a focus on testimonial manipulation, digital evidence, archival governance, and information integrity. Her broader interests include AI governance, cybersecurity policy, international humanitarian law, gender-based violence, transitional justice, and European security governance.

She will begin studies in European Governance at Vrije Universiteit Brussel while pursuing a career in European technology and security policy.

members.name: Ms Clara Jammot
members.bio:
Clara Jammot is a PhD Candidate in the Department of War Studies at King’s College London where she specializes on the nexus between international security and technology. Her doctoral research focuses on how algorithms impact ontological (in)security and perceptions of the Self within extremist communities, drawing on a mixed methods approach that reverse engineers TikTok’s algorithm through social media walkthroughs, Social Network Analysis, Python-coded sentiment analysis, and content analysis. Clara holds an MA in International Security from the Sciences Po Paris School of International Affairs with a concentration in East Asian politics and cybersecurity. She also has a BA (Hons) in Politics and International Studies from the University of Warwick.

Additionally, Clara is a part of the King’s Cyber Security Research Group where she participates in the group’s agenda-setting and research development, as well as having launched the group’s newsletter. Alongside this, she is an external expert for the Global Internet Forum to Counter Terrorism (GIFCT) as well as having advised the UK Metropolitan Police on the spread of far-right content online.

Clara has also worked for the European Cyber Security Organization (ECSO) on the Interreg Cyber Europe project and EU cyber-legislation like the NIS2 Directive, the Digital Services Act, and the Digital Markets Act. Her private sector research experience spans PwC and Kerabeo Ltd. where she research the digital transformation of society as well as conducting policy research on peacebuilding in fragile and conflict-affected states for firms consulting with the United Nations.

members.name: Dr Marius Ghincea
members.bio: Marius Ghincea is a Postdoctoral Researcher and university lecturer at ETH Zurich’s Department of Humanities, Social and Political Sciences. He received his PhD from the European University Institute in 2024, where his dissertation examined the domestic politics of foreign and security policy. Before joining ETH Zurich, he held visiting or adjunct positions at the Hertie School’s Centre for International Security, Syracuse University’s Florence program, Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) in Bologna, Central European University, George Washington University, University of Lucern, and St Antony’s College, Oxford.
keywords: Domestic Politics of Foreign and Security Policy

members.name: Prof. Monika Sus
members.bio: Monika Sus is an Associate Professor of Political Science at the Institute of Political Studies of the Polish Academy of Sciences in Warsaw and a Fellow and Adjunct at the Center for International Security at the Hertie School in Berlin. She is also a part-time Professor at the Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies at the European University Institute, where she was previously a Jean Monnet Fellow (2016–2017). Her research interests lie primarily in international relations, particularly in the study of the European Union’s foreign, security, and defence policy and in the investigation of the institutional dynamics between the supranational and national level in EU foreign policy making. Her articles have appeared in International Affairs, Journal of Common Market Studies, Geopolitics, Contemporary Security Policy, Journal of European Integration, The British Journal of Politics and International Relations, West European Politics, among others.
themes: EU, UN and other international organisations

members.name: Dr Ivan Zaccagnini
members.affiliation: ETH Zürich, Center for Security Studies
members.bio: Dr. Ivan Zaccagnini is a senior researcher in Technology and Geopolitics at the Center for Security Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich and a non-resident fellow at the Center for International and Strategic Studies (CISS) at LUISS Guido Carli university. His research interests focus on Emerging and Disruptive Technologies, Future of Warfare and Great Power Competition. His work has been published in prestigious journals including International Security, Security Studies, Contemporary Security Policy, Journal of European Integration, and Geopolitics. In April 2026 he defended his joint Ph.D. thesis entitled “Europe's Place in US–China Technology Competition. Insights from Wedging, Binding and Dynamic Sequencing” at the LUISS Guido Carli University in Rome and, for his research, he was awarded the title cum laude. The thesis was the result of a joint program between the LUISS Guido Carli University in Rome and the Centre for Security, Diplomacy and Strategy (CSDS) of the Brussels School of Governance (BSoG) at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) in Brussels. From 2020 to 2026, he was teaching assistant for International Relations and Political Risk Analysis at the Department of Political Science at LUISS University. Since 2020, he worked as Research Assistant at the Center for International and Strategic Studies (CISS-LUISS), where he is currently affiliated as a non-resident fellow. In 2022, with the financial support of the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI), he co-authored two studies on military drones and the hider-finder competition in air warfare, published respectively on International Security and Security Studies.

members.name: Dr Kire Babanoski
members.affiliation: Faculty of Security, Skopje, University "St. Kliment Ohridski", Bitola
members.bio: Kire Babanoski received his PhD in 2014 from the Faculty of Security in Skopje, University “St. Kliment Ohridski” – Bitola, North Macedonia, where he is currently an Assistant Professor. His research focuses on security studies, criminology and criminal justice, with particular emphasis on human security, regional security cooperation, and human rights in law enforcement. He also specialises in security sector governance (SSG) and security sector reform (SSR), contributing to research, policy development, and capacity-building initiatives in these fields. He has contributed as an expert to research projects supported by local civil society and international organisations, including NATO SPS, the Council of Europe, OSCE, COST, DCAF, Interreg, etc. In addition to his scholarly work, he is a licensed project manager and a certified judicial expert witness in the field of security.

members.name: Dr Alin Barbantan
members.bio:
Researcher in contemporary history and international relations, focusing on Euro-Atlantic diplomacy, US foreign policy, and Indo-Pacific strategic culture. My work examines how strategic culture and alliance networks shape the behavior of states across regions, with particular interest in comparative perspectives within the Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific areas. 

I hold a PhD in International Relations from University College London and have published research on alliance systems, strategic alignment, and regional security frameworks. I am particularly interested in collaborations, visiting research positions, and interdisciplinary projects on strategic culture and alliance systems.

members.name: Dr Daniela Mechkaroska
members.affiliation: University for Information Science and Technology “St. Paul the Apostle”
members.bio: Daniela Mechkaroska is an Assistant Professor at the University of Information Science and Technology “St. Paul the Apostle” in Ohrid, North Macedonia. Her academic and research interests include cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, cloud and edge systems, secure communication, coding theory, cryptography, and digital resilience. She is involved in university teaching, student supervision, research, and international academic cooperation. Her work focuses on the security and reliability of digital and cloud-connected systems, including AI-supported monitoring, IoT security, data integrity, and secure communication. She is particularly interested in interdisciplinary collaboration that connects emerging technologies with European security studies, institutional resilience, and trustworthy digital transformation.

members.name: Dr Eda KUŞKU SÖNMEZ
members.bio: Eda Kuşku-Sönmez holds a PhD in political science from Sabancı University, İstanbul. She is Assoc. Prof. of International Relations at Samsun University in Samsun, Turkey. Her research interests are European Union, Turkey-European Union Relations, Comparative Politics, and Turkish Foreign Policy. She previously published articles in Caucasian Review of International Affairs (2008 and 2010), and Southeast European and Black Sea Studies (2014), and Turkish Studies (2019). With Çiğdem Üstün, she coedited the book titled Turkey’s Changing Transatlantic Relations published by Lexington Books, (2021).

members.name: Dr Pınar Akgül
members.bio: Pınar Akgül is an Assistant Professor in the Department of International Relations at Giresun University, Giresun/Türkiye. Akgül earned her PhD in International Relations from University of Sussex, Brighton/UK. She holds a BA degree in International Relations from Karadeniz Teknik University, Trabzon/Türkiye and MA degree in International Relations from King’s College London, London/UK. Her research area includes studies of the Black Sea Region. Her sub-concerns are non-Western IR theories and the impact of popular culture on world politics.

members.name: Dr Tanja Pavleska
members.bio: Tanja Pavleska is a Senior Researcher at the Laboratory for Open Systems and Networks, Jožef Stefan Institute. She holds a degree in Automation and Systems Engineering and a PhD in Advanced Internet Technologies, with emphasis on user behavior in digital environments. Her research interests and expertise include the architecture design, security, and trustworthiness of digital infrastructures, information and data governance, digital policies for trust and identity management, artificial intelligence for society and society for artificial intelligence, with a focus on cybersecurity and safety. She has participated in numerous European R&I projects focused on the digital transformation of the public sector and the society in general, in view of achieving cross-border interoperability, governance, and secure service provision.

members.name: Dr Tolga Çıkrıkçı
members.bio:
I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of International Relations at Giresun University, Türkiye, where I teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Public International Law, International Human Rights Law, International Organizations, and Private International Law. I hold a PhD in International Relations, and my academic work focuses on the intersection of international law and international politics.

My research interests include international law, human rights, human security, global governance, international organizations, and contemporary security challenges. In my recent work, I have examined topics such as vaccine hesitancy and human security, discrimination and intolerance in the European Union, global justice, and the role of international law in responding to armed conflicts and international crises.

Alongside my research and teaching, I regularly present my work at national and international conferences and serve as a reviewer for academic journals in the fields of international relations and international law. I also participate in international research collaborations and contribute to academic quality assurance and accreditation processes.

Through my research, teaching, and international engagement, I aim to contribute to a deeper understanding of contemporary global challenges and the evolving role of international law and global governance in addressing them.
themes: EU, UN and other international organisations

members.name: Mr Martin Haváček
members.bio:
Martin Haváček is a doctoral researcher at the Faculty of Safety Engineering (FSE), VSB-TUO, and a research associate at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (FEECS) at the same university. His doctoral research develops neural networks for detecting security-relevant phenomena in visual data, with a focus on object detection under adverse conditions, thermal imaging, adversarial robustness of detection models, and UAV and counter-UAV detection for real-time situational awareness.

His work bridges security engineering and applied artificial intelligence. Alongside his security research, he contributes to biomedical AI projects at the LERCO centre, including ECG segmentation and biometric identification. He holds degrees in physical security engineering and in informatics and physics, and previously worked for several years as a safety technician and lecturer in occupational and fire safety, giving him a practitioner’s perspective on how detection technologies translate into operational security practice.

He also serves as an independent quality assurance evaluator for the Czech National Accreditation Bureau, the Slovak Accreditation Agency,, and is a member of IEEE and its Computational Intelligence Society.

Within NetSec he participates in WG1 and WG3, where he is interested in connecting machine learning methods for visual threat detection with the wider European security knowledge base. He welcomes collaboration on detection under adverse conditions, adversarial robustness, and the responsible deployment of AI in security-critical settings.

members.name: Dr Esra Merve Boztosun-Çalışkan
members.bio: Dr. Esra Merve Boztosun-Çalışkan is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Political Science and International Relations at Istanbul Medipol University, where she teaches courses on cybersecurity in global politics, international security, foreign policy analysis, and nationalism studies. Her research focuses on cybersecurity governance, digital sovereignty, cyber deterrence and diplomacy, and state-sponsored cyber operations, with a particular emphasis on Turkish foreign policy and the broader geopolitics of cyberspace.

members.name: Prof. David Matsaberidze
members.bio: PhD, Political Science, Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University (2015); MA, Nationalism and Ethnicity Studies, Central European University (2008). In 2015-2017 completed professional development programs on regional and international security at the George C. Marshall European Centre for Security Studies (Garmisch-Partenkirchen, Germany). In 2013-2023 served as a recurrent visiting expert with the Partnership for Peace Consortium of Defence Academies and Security Studies Institutes at the Austrian Ministry of Defence and Sports (Germany-Austria). In 2024 was awarded Ghent University’s EUREAST Platform Fellowship and was the EUREAST visiting fellow at the Institute for International and European Studies, Ghent University, Belgium. In 2008-2014 – recipient of the fellowship of the Academic Fellowship Programme, International Higher Education Support Programme and in 2011-2012  working group on frozen conflicts under the East-East Beyond Borders Program (EEBB), the Open Society Foundations (OSF) - Budapest, Hungary. Since 2023 =MC Member & WG4 Researcher at COST Action CA22121: New Rising Nationalisms, Shifting Geopolitics and the Future of European Higher Education. Research Openness (OPEN) (Brussels, Belgium) and is a Senior Research Fellow, Institute for National and International Security (Belgrade, Serbia); Since 2022 he briefs US students from various US HEIs under the SRAS - The School of Russian and Asian Studies, USA and Since 2017 he is a re-current visiting lecturer at various European universities under Erasmus+ ACM&PDP programs and lectured in Austria (2017; 2018; 2019; PoSIG 2023); Hungary (2023) and Finland (2024). Since 2017 he also serves as a member of the Academic Council. European Neighbourhood Council (ENC), Brussels, Belgium.

members.name: Prof. Islam Jusufi
members.bio: Islam Jusufi is a political science researcher and academic who is based in Skopje, North Macedonia. He holds an Associate Professorship in political science, awarded by Tirana University, Albania. Previously, he was a lecturer and department head at Epoka University, Albania. His research focuses on European and Balkan governance and security.

members.name: Mr Immanuel Rummel
members.affiliation: ETH Zürich, Center for Security Studies
members.bio: I am an early-career researcher working on issues in German and European security. I am particularly interested in Germany’s and Europe’s roles in a world of US retrenchment and geopolitical competition. My latest research project uses a network perspective to examine how non-nuclear powers restructure their deterrence when their nuclear patron retrenches.

members.name: Prof. Pavlosioannis Koktsidis
members.bio: Lectures on International Relations, Foreign Policy, Security and Conflict Resolution at the American College of Thessaloniki. Previously worked as Visiting Professor and lecturer of International Relations at the University of Cyprus. He was project manager and researcher for the externally funded program «Rearranging the Puzzle of Security in the Eastern Mediterranean: Mapping Actors and Dynamics» [2020-2023] and for the joint EU EastMed Erasmus+ programme (2016-2019). From 2019 to 2024 coordinated the annual Virginia Tech University-funded seminars programme on Conflict Studies in collaboration with the VT Department of Political Science. He is Senior Researcher at the Institute for Studies of Politics and Democracy (ISPD). His research focuses on ethnic conflict and security analysis in Southeastern Europe and the Eastern Mediterranean, state-building, war and the development of strategic thought in international relations. His work is regularly presented in international conferences, workshops and roundtable discussions (IPSA, ECPR, PSA). His research appears in internationally acclaimed peer-reviewed journals and book chapters (Journal of Ethnopolitics, Journal of Balkan and Near Eastern Studies, Eastern European Quarterly, Dynamics of Asymmetric Conflict, Civil Wars, Mediterranean Quarterly, Journal of Peace and Conflict Studies, Perspectives on Federalism, Journal of Ethnopolitics and Minority Issues in Europe). He is author of the books Ethnofederalism in Cyprus: Territory, Power and Security (Routledge: London 2024), Strategic Rebellion: Ethnic Conflict in FYR Macedonia and the Balkans (Peter Lang: Oxford 2012), and editor of the book Societies in Transition: Economic, Political and Security Transformations in Contemporary Europe (Springer, Frankfurt 2015).

members.name: Ms Giulia Biselli
members.bio:
Giulia Biselli is a Ph.D. candidate in Defence and Security Studies at the School ofAdvanced Defense Studies (CASD) and the University of Turin. She is also a Research Fellow at Geopolitica.info, where she conducts analyses on China, the Indo-Pacific, and international security.

Her research focuses on economic security, the geopolitics of critical supply chains, and strategic competition in the Indo-Pacific, with particular attention to China's foreign and economic policies and their implications for European security. Her doctoral research examines how states leverage economic, infrastructural, and institutional instruments to generate long-term strategic influence below the threshold of armed conflict.

Alongside her academic work, Giulia is the founder and director of a Switzerland-based consultancy specializing in human rights, responsible supply chains, and social sustainability. She has extensive expertise in human rights investigations and due diligence across global supply chains, advising organizations on social and geopolitical risks. She also delivers training on business and human rights, women's rights, DEI, and the protection of vulnerable and minority groups.

This professional experience provides a practical dimension to her academic research, offering first-hand insight into the governance challenges, strategic vulnerabilities, and resilience of critical supply chains.

members.name: Prof. Paulina Polko
members.position: Head of the Security Studies Department
members.bio:
Correspondence address: WSB University, Cieplaka 1c, 41-300 Dabrowa Gornicza, Poland

2001: MA, University of Warsaw, Poland, Political Studies Department
2010: PhD, Polish Academy of Science, Institute of Political Studies. Dissertation: Enlightened oligarchic monarchy – Italy under Silvio Berlusconi's rule
2023: DSc, WSB University. Main research achievement: Security in Polish political discourse (1989-2020). 
2023: associate professor at WSB University

Scientific fields of interest: critical security studies, national security, security policy, migration-security nexus, security discourse. Author or co-author of over 70 publications on different aspects related to security studies. 

In the field of migration-security nexus, she employs a flexible approach that proposes more complex research, focusing not only on the perspective of the destination country (state/nation/social groups/individual) but also on the perspective of the country (nation) of origin and immigrants as individuals. This perspective has not been widely recognised in recent security studies. In Poland, she has already initiated the project and comparative research on the security perception of three waves of Ukrainian migrants (before 2014, 2014-2022, and after Feb. 24, 2022).

In the field of securitisation and critical security studies, she focuses on deepening the assessment and evaluation of securitisation processes at both the theoretical and empirical levels. 

In the field of national security systems, she focuses on institutional cooperation and collaboration, as well as evaluating the efficiency of systemic solutions. 

Member of the Polish Society of Security Studies, Polish Geopolitical Society and European Initiative for Security Studies – EISS.

members.name: Dr Mehmet Babacan
members.bio: Mehmet BABACAN was awarded his PhD degree in Middle East Studies from the Department of International Relations at Bursa Uludag University. With numerous national and international publications in the fields of international politics, Turkish foreign policy, Middle East Studies and Jerusalem and Palestinian studies, Babacan currently serves at Yıldız Technical University. Babacan, who has served as an expert and researcher on numerous YOK (Turkish Higher Education Council) and EU (European Union) projects, is married, has three children and speaks Turkish, English, Arabic.

members.name: Dr Gayane Harutyunyan
members.affiliation: Public Administration Academy of the Republic of Armenia
members.bio: Gayane Harutyunyan is the vice-rector for scientific affairs of the Public Administration Academy of the Republic of Armenia. She is also part-time research fellow of the Strategic Games and Simulation Group of the National Defense Research University of the Ministry of Defense of the Republic of Armenia. Her academic and research work covers more than 70 research papers on defense economics, military and economic security, international economic relations, defense resources management, green defense industry, military use of artificial intelligence, 3 monographs, 5 teaching manuals, over 20 papers for local and international conferences and workshops. During past ten years she was also а research team leader of five scientific projects funding by the Science Committee of the Republic of Armenia within the framework of contractual (thematic) financing of the scientific and scientific-technical activities.
